case_name: Jagat Singh v State of Haryana
respondent:
State of Haryana
Supreme Court of India

4 November 1976
Cr.A. No. 248 of 1975 [Arising as an appeal by Special Leave from the Judgment and Order Dt. 6 February 1975 of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Cr. Appeal 398 of 1974].
The Judgment was delivered by: GUPTA, J.
1.  The Appellant Jagat Singh was convicted by the Additional Sessions Judge, Jind, u/s. 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced to death. He was further convicted u/s. 324 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and S. 27 of the Arms Act and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for one year and two years respectively. The High Court of Punjab and Haryana hearing the appeal preferred by Jagat Singh against his conviction and the reference for confirmation of the sentence of death passed on him, maintained his conviction but commuted the sentence of death to one for imprisonment for life. This appeal by special leave preferred by Jagat Singh is limited to the ground whether the offence fell u/s. 304
facts: The Appellant Jagat Singh was convicted by the Additional Sessions Judge, Jind, u/s. 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced to death.

On February 14, 1973 at 12.40 p.m. Umed Singh, a student of that college, was hit on the chest and right thigh in the college premises by two shots fired in quick succession by Jagat Singh from his gun.
The management of the college charged the students of 1972-73 batch Rs. 20 each for supplying sportswear.
A batch of students gathered in the college compound and decided to demand an account from the college authorities.
Hukam Singh assured the students that the accounts would be placed before them the next day when the principal of the college was to join duty.
The students then marched in a body to the appellant's office, called him out and demanded accounts.
It appears that the appellant managed to go to his residential quarter which was at a distance of about 100 yards from his office and came armed with a 12 bore gun.
A political worker who was not a student was seen addressing the students on the college lawns exhorting them to stay away from the classes, and the appellant trying to catch him gave him a chase.
One of the slogans raised by the students was 'dismiss Jagat Singh'.
The High Court further found that the prosecution witnesses had concealed the real origin of the incident and what 'actually happened when they (students) confronted the appellant'.
petitioner_arguments: The plea taken by the appellant was that he was encircled and manhandled by the students and in that melee the gun accidentally went off.
court_reasoning: The High Court observed further that the appellant was a normal man, in possession of normal faculties and was 'not expected to embark upon such a hazardous path to fire shots without any provocation'.

It seems to us that the circumstances as found by the High Court are not merely a valid ground for commuting the sentence of death to one for imprisonment for life but also bear upon the nature of the offence.
On the findings of the High Court we hold that the case comes under the first part of S. 304 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and not S. 302.
holding: The appeal is allowed to the extent indicated above.
We order accordingly. The appeal is allowed to the extent indicated above.
